summary: Haje Jan Kamps's Startups Weekly newsletter opens with the question of whether events are worth it for founders, citing a TC+ survey of more than 50 founders that found no real consensus, only pros and cons. The rest is a roundup of the week's tech news: AI (OpenAI chip rumors, Adobe Firefly, Tidalflow), hardware (Meta Quest 3, Pixel 8, PC shipments), social platforms (Reddit, Mastodon, X, VidCon) and top reads on Google passkeys, Mastercard on UPI, and Brave layoffs.
one_line: Startups Weekly asks whether events are worth founders' time, citing a TC+ survey of 50+ founders, then rounds up the week's AI, hardware and social news.
key_facts: Reddit co-founder Alexis Ohanian tweeted that if he could redo one thing when building Reddit, he would have spent significantly less time attending events.
Haje Jan Kamps says he always regrets traveling to an event beforehand but never regrets it on the way back, since something magical comes out of going.
The TC+ team surveyed more than 50 founders on whether attending events still makes sense in 2023, and found no real consensus but useful pros and cons.
Kamps wrote this newsletter while laid up at home with pneumonia.
Rumors say OpenAI may be considering developing its own AI chips; ChatGPT's mobile app hit a record $4.6 million in revenue last month, but growth is slowing.
Dutch startup Tidalflow exited stealth with backing from Google's Gradient Ventures, aiming to help any software work with ChatGPT and other LLM ecosystems.
Adobe is doubling down on its Firefly generative AI models and showed Project Stardust as a sneak preview of its next-gen AI photo editing engine.
A federal judge threw out Sonos's $32.5 million win against Google after the company's patents were deemed unenforceable and invalid.
Ron reports that PC shipments decline slowed in Q3 2023 and that Apple's sales plunged over 23%.
Mastodon has 407K+ more monthly users than it thought, but its peak is now about the same as a decade ago.
X (formerly Twitter) is testing three tiers of its Premium service, and code suggests one tier may be ad-free.
Google is making passkeys the default sign-in method for all users.
Mastercard CFO Sachin Mehra praised UPI for helping digitization in India but called it an "incredibly painful experience" for ecosystem participants and questioned its commercial sustainability.
Brave Software, maker of Brave Browser and Search, laid off 9% of its workforce across departments.
VidCon hosted its first industry leadership summit, where creator economy experts and creators discussed grievances and ideas to make a creator's job more sustainable.
